Capacity Planner

Feature

Preview: You can use the Capacity Planner remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (capacityplanner.googleapis.com) to connect AI applications and agents to your Capacity Planner data (Preview). You can use the Capacity Planner MCP tools to query historical resource usage, usage forecasts, and reservation data across your projects, folders, and organizations.

For more information, see the Capacity Planner MCP reference and Google Cloud MCP servers overview.

Cloud Database Migration Service

Feature

You can now create heterogeneous conversion workspaces by importing database schema metadata files from a Cloud Storage bucket without requiring direct network connectivity between Database Migration Service and your source database during the schema conversion phase. For more information, see the following pages:

  • Create a conversion workspace for Oracle to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL
  • Create a conversion workspace for Oracle to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
  • Create a conversion workspace for SQL Server to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL
  • Create a conversion workspace for SQL Server to AlloyDB for PostgreSQL

Compute Engine

Security

A vulnerability (CVE-2026-85299) about incorrect authorization in Compute Engine was discovered and has been addressed. For more information, see the GCP-2026-073 security bulletin.

Developer Connect

Feature

The Developer Connect Model Context Protocol (MCP) server is available in Preview.

AI applications and coding assistants can use the Developer Connect MCP server to read commits, diffs, file blame, and pull requests. They can also open, update, and comment on pull requests in repositories that you link from GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, and GitLab Enterprise.

The same operations are available as GitRepositoryLink methods in the Developer Connect REST API.

For more information, see the Developer Connect MCP reference.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

Control user intent matching for semantic governance policies

You can now turn user intent matching on or off for semantic governance policies by setting the sgpUserIntentMatching key on the authorization extension metadata. User intent matching is on by default; set the key to DISABLED to turn it off. Turning it off reduces protection against indirect prompt injection. When the key is set, policy evaluation logs report the mode each evaluation used in the sgpUserIntentMatchingMode field.

For more information, see Control user intent matching.

Feature

Cloud Storage output support for Gemini image generation models

Direct Cloud Storage output persistence is generally available (GA) for Gemini Nano Banana 2.1 (gemini-nano-banana-2.1), Gemini 3.1 Flash Image (gemini-3.1-flash-image), Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image (gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image), and Gemini 3 Pro Image (gemini-3-pro-image). You can set outputConfig.outputUriPrefix and generationConfig.responseFormat[].image.delivery to "URI" in generateContent and streamGenerateContent requests to write generated and edited images directly to a Cloud Storage bucket and receive the object URI in fileData.fileUri instead of inline bytes. For more information, see Save generated images to Cloud Storage.

Feature

Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS are Generally Available (GA)

Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS are available in General Availability (GA) in the global location and the us and eu multi-regions. The models support structured speaker and style metadata, inline vocal tags, multi-speaker dialogue, and streaming. Voice design and voice replication capabilities remain available in Preview.

For more information, see Generate speech with Gemini TTS.

Feature

Semantic governance policies support more model providers

Semantic governance policies now evaluate tool calls from agents that use models from providers other than Gemini. The policy engine reads each provider's request and response format, so the same policies apply whichever model your agent uses. Supported APIs include the Gemini Developer API and Gemini models on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, the Anthropic Messages API, Claude models on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, the OpenAI Chat Completions API, the Mistral AI API, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (including Llama models), and self-hosted OpenAI-compatible servers such as vLLM. Streamed model responses aren't supported.

To govern these providers, update the when condition of your authorization policy to match each provider's request path. The updated condition also matches requests that include a query string.

For more information, see Supported model providers and Connect the policy engine to Agent Gateway.

Knowledge Catalog

Feature

Support for Looker (Google Cloud core) in Data lineage is now generally available. This support includes lineage views for LookML views and Explores, Looker dashboards, dashboard elements, Looks, LookML dashboards, and Conversational Analytics agents. You can control data lineage ingestion at the organization, folder, and project levels. You can also visualize the end-to-end flow of your data from BigQuery sources through the Looker semantic layer to downstream assets.

For more information, see Track data lineage with Knowledge Catalog, About data lineage, and About data lineage ingestion control.

Looker

Feature

Looker (Google Cloud core) data lineage is now generally available (GA). The GA launch adds end-to-end visibility for LookML dashboards and Conversational Analytics agents. Lineage enablement is now managed independently through the Data Lineage API and service-level ingestion controls, which decouples it from Looker's internal Knowledge Catalog metadata settings. For more information, see About data lineage.

Feature

The Looker-managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) server is now generally available (GA), allowing AI agents to securely interact with business data and LookML models without the need for additional middleware. This launch is supported by a new Manage OAuth Clients admin page, which provides a centralized interface for governing identity-based access for AI agents and other external applications. Administrators can now quickly enable pre-configured integrations from the Application Library or register custom OAuth clients with specific redirect URIs and group-based access controls.

Model Armor

Feature

Model Armor enforces the constraints/modelarmor.managed.requireTemplateDataResidencyCompliance managed Organization Policy Service constraint by default. When you create or update a template, this constraint prevents you from setting data_residency_compliant to false or clearing the Enforce data residency option unless an Organization Policy Administrator disables the constraint. This feature is generally available (GA). For more information, see Disable the organization policy constraint for data residency.

Oracle Database@Google Cloud

Feature

The Oracle Database@Google Cloud remote MCP server is generally available (GA) and adds tools to create and manage Database Connections and run SQL statements with database_connection_executesql. It lets you interact easily with Oracle Database@Google Cloud resources from LLMs, AI applications, and AI-enabled development platforms.

For more information, see Use the Oracle Database@Google Cloud remote MCP server.

Additionally, AlloyDB AI adds pre-registered support for the semantic-ranker-512 reranking model.

For more information, see Pre-registered Agent Platform models.

Apigee hybrid

Announcement

v1.17.3

On October 29, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.17.3.

  • For information on upgrading, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid to version v1.17.3.
  • For information on new installations, see The big picture.
Note: Do not use Apigee hybrid v1.17.2 due to a potential regression in apigee-connect-agent (see known issue 578314600). Use v1.17.3 instead.
Note: This is a patch release: The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch via the Helm chart automatically updates the images. No manual image changes are typically needed. For information on container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see Apigee release process.

Feature

New ApigeeValkey custom resource

Apigee hybrid v1.17.3 adds the ApigeeValkey custom resource definition (CRD), the apigee-valkey Helm chart, and the valkey configuration properties. ApigeeValkey is the replacement for the ApigeeRedis resource.

In version 1.17.3, the runtime continues to use ApigeeRedis. When you upgrade, install the new CRD with the other CRDs. Leave the new ao.args.valkeyBackend property set to its default value, false. You don't need to install the apigee-valkey chart or change your configuration.

For the supported upgrade sequence, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid. For more information about the resource, see Kubernetes resources.

Fixed

Fixed in this release

Bug ID Description
578314600 Fixed an issue where apigee-connect-agent ignored HTTPS_PROXY and failed to establish a tether in clusters that require an HTTP forward proxy for egress; the agent now uses HTTP/2 keepalive pings on the control-plane connection while honoring HTTPS_PROXY (including proxy credentials).
576707253 Removed the compromised emSign roots and the cross-signing Comodo AAA Services root from the system and Java (cacerts) trust stores across containers.
573622417 Fixed an issue where apigee-ingressgateway forwarded the x-envoy-decorator-operation header to upstream runtime and target backends.
572025634 Fixed an issue where responses with a compressed text/event-stream body to a proxy with an EventFlow returned a corrupted body; compressed text/event-stream responses now skip EventFlow processing and pass through intact.
571378258 The apigee-redis container now uses the Valkey engine (version 8.1.10). The RESP2 wire protocol and redis-server and redis-cli binary names are unchanged.
568860869 Fixed an issue in the RegularExpressionProtection policy where patterns starting and ending with .* whose middle section contained regular expression syntax were matched as literal text instead of regular expressions.
560272924 Apigee hybrid now supports continuous-scan bidirectional gRPC streaming for the SanitizeModelResponse policy over Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams, preserving native LLM provider SSE JSON envelopes and event framing.
555332621 Fixed an issue where Model Armor policies did not honor HTTPClient.managementplane.skip.proxy: when set, Model Armor callouts now bypass the forward proxy like other googleapis traffic, while streaming (ContinuousScan) Model Armor traffic uses the forward proxy.
554114419 Fixed an issue where an AssignMessage, HTTPModifier, or RaiseFault policy that creates a new request (createNew="true") in an HTTP/2 flow could not set the :path and :authority pseudo-headers and failed with an invalid-header error.
549779897 Apigee analytics now reports the Model Armor template, verdict, and matched filters for each request on both the prompt and model-response directions.
546141116 The SemanticCacheLookup policy now reports the cache key and cache name to analytics in the ai_semantic_cache_key and ai_semantic_cache_name fields.
535395491 Extension Processor (ext_proc) denials now return the status and body that the policy or FaultRule produced, instead of always returning HTTP 500.
524115876 Fixed an intermittent HTTP 400 error in the OASValidation policy's strict parameter validation that rejected valid requests under load.
502231886 Fixed an issue where the SanitizeUserPrompt and SanitizeModelResponse policies failed to extract content using default source templates when the <Source> element was omitted and <IgnoreUnresolvedVariables> was set to false.
492041991 Fixed an issue where VerifyAPIKey and VerifyAccessToken set the apiproduct.operation.llmTokenQuota.* flow variables from unmatched LLM operations; they are now set only from the LLM operations that matched the request.
449228485 Fixed an issue where podDisruptionBudget overrides configured in the Helm charts were dropped by the Kubernetes API server.

Cloud Profiler

Security

The Cloud Profiler Java agent is updated with a new Certification Authority (CA) certificate bundle, in response to security bulletin GCP-2026-071. Google Cloud infrastructure and the Cloud Profiler backend service are not affected.

If you use the Cloud Profiler Java agent, take one of the following actions:

  • Upgrade the Java agent to cloud-profiler-java-agent_20261026_RC00 (GitHub release v0.5.0) or later, and then rebuild and redeploy your applications. Download the updated archive, https://storage.googleapis.com/cloud-profiler/java/cloud-profiler-java-agent_20261026_RC00.tar.gz, or, for musl-based Alpine Linux containers, https://storage.googleapis.com/cloud-profiler/java/cloud-profiler-java-agent_20261026_RC00_alpine.tar.gz.
  • If you can't immediately upgrade or rebuild, update your host or container operating system's CA certificate store as described in GCP-2026-071, and then set the GRPC_DEFAULT_SSL_ROOTS_FILE_PATH environment variable to point to the updated PEM bundle.

For more information about installing the agent, see Profiling Java applications.

Dataflow

Feature

Dataflow has added the following features to tune horizontal autoscaling for Streaming Engine jobs:

  • Latency tiers: You can configure the backlog threshold by choosing a latency tier (low_latency, medium_latency, or high_latency), allowing you to configure the autoscaler's sensitivity to backlog duration and balance latency requirements with resource costs. For more information, see Set the latency tier.
  • Autoscaling schedules: You can configure recurring autoscaling schedules to automatically apply parameter overrides—such as minimum and maximum workers, worker utilization hints, or latency tiers—during specific time windows. For more information, see Schedule autoscaling changes.

You can configure these features when you create a job or update them while the job is running.

Announcement

Security

Dialogflow ES: The Dialogflow ES LINE integration validates the X-Line-Signature HTTP header on incoming webhook requests using your LINE channel secret and rejects requests with missing, duplicate, or invalid signatures with an HTTP 400 Bad Request error. Make sure your configured channel secret matches your LINE Messaging API channel and that any intermediate proxy forwards the X-Line-Signature header and raw request body unmodified.

Google Kubernetes Engine

Feature

Managed OpenTelemetry for GKE is generally available (GA) on clusters running GKE version 1.37.1-gke.1697000 or later. You can collect OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) traces, metrics, and logs from your workloads with a Google-managed collector instead of a self-managed OpenTelemetry Collector deployment:

  • Configure otlp_grpc in the Instrumentation custom resource (GKE version 1.37.1-gke.1697000 or later), or send telemetry directly to the in-cluster collector's gRPC endpoint on port 4317 in addition to HTTP on port 4318.
  • The managed collector routes logs alongside traces and metrics through the Cloud Telemetry API (telemetry.googleapis.com), with improved per-signal queueing and autoscaling for high-throughput clusters. (Logs ingested through telemetry.googleapis.com default to the otlp log name instead of gke-managed-otel-collector.)
  • Multimodal prompts and responses collection for LangGraph ReAct and Agent Development Kit (ADK) agents, the --managed-otel-scope flag in the gcloud CLI (version 576.0.0 or later), and managed_opentelemetry_config in terraform-provider-google (v8.8.0 or later) are generally available.

To use the GA collector and features, upgrade clusters from earlier Preview versions to 1.37.1-gke.1697000 or later. For architecture details and setup instructions, see Managed OpenTelemetry for GKE and Deploy Managed OpenTelemetry for GKE.

Identity and Access Management

Feature

The Admin (roles/admin), Writer (roles/writer), and Reader (roles/reader) basic roles are generally available (GA). For more information, see Basic roles.

The legacy basic roles—Owner (roles/owner), Editor (roles/editor), and Viewer (roles/viewer)—are still available for use and are being actively maintained. However, if you need to grant a basic role, we recommend granting the Admin, Writer, or Reader role instead of a legacy basic role. This is because the newer roles support additional features, such as the use of IAM Conditions.

Looker

Announcement

Beginning October 26, 2026, the following features will be automatically enabled for Looker (original) and Looker (Google Cloud core) instances running Looker 26.20.

Feature

The ability to generate a summary of an Explore by using Gemini assistance is now generally available.

Feature

The bullet chart visualization type is now generally available. Bullet charts let you evaluate a single primary metric's performance as one or more bars and mark your goal with a target line. You can plot both against shaded background ranges that represent performance thresholds, such as "poor," "satisfactory," and "good." For more information, see Bullet chart options.

Feature

Looker now includes network diagnostics to help you troubleshoot database connectivity issues. When a database connection test fails, Looker automatically tests DNS resolution and TCP connectivity for the connection's endpoints and appends the results to the error message. To test network reachability to any hostname and port without creating a connection, Looker administrators can click Test Reachability on the Connections page.

Note: This item was added on October 30, 2026.

Feature

The Table Row Grouping feature and the Grouping menu options are now generally available. The Grouping menu options let you display and customize the appearance of table chart data hierarchically in groups.

Feature

The Visualization Assistant is now generally available.

Feature

Looker Continuous Integration (CI) now supports hub-and-spoke projects. If your Looker project uses local project imports to import files from an upstream hub project on the same Looker instance, then you can use CI to automatically test downstream spoke projects. Testing runs whenever a pull request is opened or updated on the hub project. This capability lets you catch breaking changes in downstream Explores, content, or data tests before upstream LookML changes are merged. For more information, see Creating a Continuous Integration suite.

Feature

Two new legacy features, Use Legacy Explore and Merge Query Experience and Use Legacy Explore and Merge Query Experience for Embed, are now available for Looker (original) and Looker (Google Cloud core) instances. These features let administrators configure Explores and merged queries to open in the classic experience by default across an instance or in embedded contexts. For more information, see Legacy feature schedule.

Feature

Looker now includes a new histogram chart visualization option. A histogram chart is a graphical representation of the data distribution of an attribute. A histogram creates intervals (bins) and counts how many values fall into each bin.

Feature

The KPI (Single Value) chart type is now generally available. The KPI (Single Value) chart type replaces the Single Value chart type.

Feature

The new Looker Explore and merge query experience is now generally available and is the default interface for Explores and for joining data from multiple queries.

Feature

When you enter values in a string filter on dashboards, Looks, or Explores, clicking Done or clicking outside the input field no longer creates a filter chip from uncommitted text. To create a filter chip, press Enter, enter a comma (,), or paste values into the input field.

Feature

The new Dashboard Tile Groups preview feature lets you organize related tiles into collapsible containers for improved visual organization. You can move, duplicate, or delete multiple tiles as a single unit on dashboards that use the newspaper layout. This update also adds LookML support for programmatically managing tile groups.

Feature

Now available in preview, the Release Changelog gives Looker users and administrators real-time visibility into the features, behavioral changes, and bug fixes that are available for their instance.

Feature

The Legacy features page is now available in the Admin panel for Looker (Google Cloud core) instances. Legacy features that appear on the Looker (Google Cloud core) Legacy features page might differ from those that are available on Looker (original) instances. For more information, see Looker (Google Cloud core) admin settings.

Announcement

The latest versions in the Looker (Google Cloud core) release channels are beginning deployment as follows:

  • Latest version in the Rapid channel: Looker 26.22
  • Latest version in the No Channel channel: Looker 26.22

The latest version in the Regular channel remains Looker 26.18.

Breaking

Some elements of the Conversational Analytics System Activity dashboard have been renamed. The dashboard layout and capabilities remain the same.

On the Token usage tab, the Conversational Analytics API value in the Feature column and the Feature Name filter has been renamed to Looker API. This value refers to the Conversational Analytics methods for the Looker API.

This rename might cause a breaking change if you built custom dashboards that reference the former Feature column or Feature Name filter value.

Change

The Use Legacy Connections Page legacy feature and the legacy database connection workflow have been removed. All database connections now use the connection workflow that is described in Connecting Looker to your database.

Google SecOps

Feature

Basic Mode search

This feature is in public preview. The SIEM Search page now provides two search-execution modes: Basic Mode and Advanced Mode. Basic Mode (the default option) uses a streamlined, fast-path execution pipeline that bypasses secondary enrichment steps during search execution. This approach reduces end-to-end search wait times while preserving full data fidelity and query syntax parity. Advanced Mode is equivalent to the previous search experience.

For more information, see Choose the search-execution mode and Understand the search-execution modes.

API Gateway

Feature

MCP method and tool name in request logs

API Gateway request logs now include the Model Context Protocol (MCP) method of each MCP request, and the tool name of each tools/call request, in the jsonPayload.mcp field. You can use this field to find MCP traffic and the calls to a specific tool.

For more information, see Configure Model Context Protocol.

Feature

TLS 1.3 for connections to backends

API Gateway is rolling out support for TLS 1.3 on connections to backend services. Once the rollout reaches a gateway, it uses TLS 1.3 with backends that support it. No configuration is required.

Agent Platform Workbench

Feature

Antigravity CLI in Agent Platform Workbench instances

Preview: The Antigravity CLI is available in Agent Platform Workbench instances that use a Debian 12 (workbench-instances-2603) or later image. The Antigravity CLI is the terminal surface of Google Antigravity, an AI agent that works in a terminal. New instances have it turned on by default. You can use the Antigravity CLI to do tasks like the following:

  • Create, explain, edit, check, and run notebooks.
  • Create a Jupyter kernel with the packages that you need.
  • Run shell commands and Google Cloud commands, such as gcloud and bq.
  • Write the code for a notebook cell from a description, with the %%agy cell magic.

The Antigravity CLI asks for your approval before it edits a file or runs a command. To turn it off for an instance, set the enable-antigravity metadata key to false. To get started, see Use the Antigravity CLI.

BigQuery

Feature

You can use graph measures to lock an aggregation to a key in order to perform complex aggregations without overcounting. Measure expressions can include the following:

  • Aggregate function calls
  • Expressions within aggregate functions
  • Conditional logic within aggregate functions
  • Conditional distinct counting
  • Scalar operations and expressions outside of aggregate functions
  • Combinations of measures wrapped in the AGG function

To query measures, you transform your graph into a flattened table by using the GRAPH_EXPAND TVF, and then query measures in that table with the AGG function. The GRAPH_EXPAND function now supports multiple fact tables. To view the output schema of the GRAPH_EXPAND function, use the BQ.SHOW_GRAPH_EXPAND_SCHEMA system procedure.

You can define extensions in the OPTIONS clause of the labels and properties in your graphs, which are string pairs that represent custom metadata for natural language querying.

Measures and graphs are supported in Data Studio through the BigQuery connector. Measures and graphs are also automatically cataloged in Knowledge Catalog, which makes them searchable by natural language or domain synonyms.

These features are generally available (GA).

Feature

BigQuery generative AI functions now support the gemini-4-carbon model. This model is generally available.

Cloud Billing

Feature

Estimate costs for AI agents using the new cost estimator agent (Preview)

Cloud Billing is introducing cost estimation directly inside the Billing section of the Google Cloud console, starting with cost estimation for AI agents now available in Preview.

Using the new Cost estimator agent, you can generate high-level estimates based on reference architectures for agents built with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, helping you understand the potential cost of your agent before you build it.

To get cost estimates for your planned Google Cloud workloads and other cloud infrastructure, you can also use the Google Cloud pricing calculator. With the pricing calculator, you can estimate costs for a wide range of Google Cloud services and products.

Cost estimates help you set spend caps, create Cloud Billing budgets and alerts, allocate project quotas, and get financial sign-off for a launch.

For more information about the cost estimator tools, see the following:

  • Cost estimator agent
  • Pricing calculator

Cloud Logging

Feature

VM Extension Manager extension policies for the Ops Agent are now available at the folder and organization levels in Preview. Extension policies provide zonal and global Ops Agent installation, version upgrades, and configuration management. For more information, see VM Extension Manager policies for the Ops Agent.

In addition, new read-only APIs are available in Preview for querying the details and status of installed VM extensions. For more information, see View extension details and status.

Compute Engine

Feature

For your regional managed instance groups (MIGs), you can view planned instance allocations across zones and machine types, check the number of instances waiting for capacity, and configure alerts based on this data. Compute Engine records these details in instance distribution logs in Cloud Logging when you create a regional MIG or increase its target size. For more information, see View instance distribution logs.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 4 Carbon available in web app, mobile app, Workflow Builder, and AI developer tools

Gemini 4 Carbon is generally available (GA) for the Gemini Enterprise web app, mobile app, Workflow Builder, and AI developer tools.

  • Location availability: Supported in global, us, and eu multi-regions, with data residency and ML processing support in us and eu. For more information, see Data residency for Gemini Enterprise.
  • App availability: Turned off by default. Gemini 4 Carbon is supported in the web app and mobile app. For more information about turning on the model, see Manage features on the web app.
  • Workflow Builder: Gemini 4 Carbon is available in Workflow Builder. For more information, see Workflow Builder.
  • AI developer tools: Enabled by default for licensed users when Antigravity authorized models uses the default selection. If your organization specifies a custom model list, an administrator must manually select Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information, see Configure AI developer tools settings.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

Cross-project governance for semantic governance policies

You can use semantic governance policies in a multi-project (hub-and-spoke) architecture to centrally govern agents deployed across multiple Google Cloud projects. When you configure a Resource Manager management boundary with the AGENT_MANAGEMENT capability, Agent Registry in the central management project automatically discovers agents across all member projects with their runtime identities intact. You can then provision a single Agent Gateway and semantic governance policy engine in the management project to author and enforce policies across member project agents.

For more information, see Govern agents across multiple projects and Cross-project boundaries.

Feature

Provisioned Throughput supports more detailed order statuses

Provisioned Throughput supports more granular order statuses in the Google Cloud console in General Availability (GA). You can track order lifecycle states across Declined, Cancelled, and Terminated, in addition to Pending review, Approved, Active, and Expired. For more information, see Check order status.

Fixed

CodeMender updates (v0.20.0)

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  • Bug fixes:
    • Fixed patch application failures during validation on large repositories and projects with mixed LF and CRLF line endings.
    • Fixed scan error handling to properly surface permission denied errors when scanning unreadable directories instead of reporting zero findings.

For more information, see the CodeMender documentation.

Feature

Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber (GA)

Gemini 4 Carbon (gemini-4-carbon) and Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber (gemini-4-carbon-cyber-permissive) are generally available (GA). Gemini 4 Carbon is Google's frontier model for complex, real-world tasks across coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science, with a unified 1,048,576-token input and output limit, long decodes up to 1,048,576 tokens using continuation_token, configurable thinking levels (LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH), implicit context caching with durable caching, Microsoft Office and OpenDocument file inputs, and Provisioned Throughput support. Gemini 4 Carbon for cyber is a defensive cybersecurity variant available behind the Fairwind Program allowlist.

Managed Service for Apache Airflow

Breaking

(Airflow 3.3.1, 3.2.2, and 2.11.1) Upgraded the pip package from version 23.2.1 to version 26.2.2. This update is available in Managed Airflow (Gen 3) builds composer-3-airflow-3.3.1-build.8, composer-3-airflow-3.2.2-build.12, and composer-3-airflow-2.11.1-build.25 and later, and in the Managed Airflow (Gen 2) image composer-2.18.0-airflow-2.11.1 and later.

This version includes security fixes and changes how custom PyPI packages are installed:

  • PEP 440 version specifiers: pip 26.2.2 enforces PEP 440 compliance and supports the .* wildcard only with == and !=. For example, use gcsfs>=0.8 instead of gcsfs>=0.8.*.
  • Isolated source builds: source packages (.tar.gz) are always built in an isolated environment. If you install source packages from a private repository that is your only package index, make sure that the repository contains precompiled wheel packages (.whl) for setuptools and any other build dependencies (listed under [build-system] requires in pyproject.toml). Alternatively, publish your packages as .whl packages. As a temporary workaround to disable build isolation, add no-build-isolation = false to the [global] section of your pip.conf file. This workaround works only if the build dependencies are already installed in your environment.
  • Legacy pkg_resources builds: older source packages that rely on pkg_resources might fail to build. Use newer package versions with precompiled .whl packages, or for your own private packages, build them as .whl packages or update their build scripts so that they don't use the legacy pkg_resources module.

Make sure that your custom PyPI packages are compatible with these changes before you upgrade your environment. If the installation of PyPI packages fails during an upgrade, your environment keeps running with its current version and packages.

Feature

Agent Search: Search-as-you-type for custom search apps (Preview)

You can configure schema fields to support search-as-you-type in custom search apps. Search-as-you-type returns a refreshed set of ranked documents on every keystroke before a user finishes typing a full query. Unlike autocomplete, which suggests query strings, search-as-you-type returns matching documents so that users can browse an updating result list and find the right result mid-query.

This feature is in Public Preview. For more information, see Configure field settings.

Announcement

On November 13, 2026, we released an updated version of Apigee (1-18-0-apigee-9).

Note: Rollouts of this release began today and can take four or more business days to complete across all Google Cloud zones. Your instances might not have the features and fixes available until the rollout is complete.

Security

Bug ID Description
579640924 Security fix for Apigee. Hardened the JavaCallout, Script, and JavaScript policy sandboxes.
579642864 Security fix for Apigee. Fixed an OAuth 2.0 redirect_uri validation bypass in non-strict sub-resource matching and enforced <EnforceStrictCallbackURI> on GenerateAuthorizationCode policies.
579642568 Security fix for Apigee. Fixed a Jython sandbox escape where user-supplied <JythonURL> JARs defining org.python.core.PyReflected classes received the unrestricted pythonns: protection domain.
582347995, 577964152 Security fix for Apigee. Upgraded the ingress gateway to patch security vulnerabilities.
N/A Security fix for Apigee infrastructure.

Fixed

Bug ID Description
582789138 Added the response.event.stream.state and response.event.stream.content.length flow variables on SSE EventFlow responses, readable in PostClientFlow so a MessageLogging step can distinguish COMPLETE, UPSTREAM_ABORT, DOWNSTREAM_ABORT, and TIMEOUT terminations and log bytes sent. Use with response.event.processed.count for the per-stream event count.
582791025 WS-Security signing with SignatureConfirmation values no longer duplicates or fails, and signed confirmations and other signed elements now validate.
582790275 WS-Security signature validation with max_lifetime no longer rejects every document.
582790249 Debug traces no longer drop the Execution entry of a policy that fails with an exception that has no message.
582790971 Debug sessions no longer show unmasked payloads, query parameters, headers, or flow variables when another session or a masking error intervenes.
582790557 Management API paths now match registered base paths on whole path segments only; for example, /optimizer no longer routes to the /o resource.
583643203 The SanitizeUserPrompt and SanitizeModelResponse policies now forward the MA-Client-Correlation-Id header to Model Armor.
579213551 Fixed Message Processor memory leaks during proxy deployment and environment reload. Compiled OASValidation specifications are shared by content hash, and resources of superseded or failed environment loads are released.
583672651 Fixed a connection count leak in the runtime HTTP server on management ports (for example, 8843) that could inflate the autoscaling metric and pin runtime replicas at the maximum, exhausting cluster CPU.
568062600 Semantic Governance traces now record the LLM family and model of each request, including requests it skips.
576448578 Fixed an issue where streamed target responses lasting longer than the inbound connection timeout (120s) could be truncated when the proxy endpoint buffered a large request body.
572000222 Apigee distributed-trace spans on the Envoy ext_proc path now continue the caller's inbound W3C or B3 trace context instead of starting a new trace.
N/A Updates to infrastructure and libraries.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: 3-legged OAuth authentication with Agent Identity auth manager for A2A agents

Support for 3-legged OAuth (3LO) authentication with Agent Identity auth manager for Agent2Agent (A2A) agents is generally available (GA).

This integration lets A2A agents built with the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and deployed on Agent Runtime authenticate to downstream Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, Google Cloud services, and third-party APIs on behalf of the signed-in Gemini Enterprise user. When a tool requires user consent, Gemini Enterprise automatically prompts the user, validates the callback at https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/validateUserId, finalizes credentials with Agent Identity auth manager, and resumes the A2A conversation.

For more information, see the following resources:

  • Configure 3-legged OAuth with Agent Identity auth manager for A2A agents
  • Authenticate using 3-legged OAuth with auth manager

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Single-user quota limits for AI developer tools

Single-user quota limits apply to AI developer tools, including Google Antigravity, in the Gemini Enterprise Standard and Gemini Enterprise Plus editions. For AI developer tools, the quota multiplier applies to the weekly quota and resets on each user's seven-day cycle.

This feature is generally available (GA). For more information, see Single-user quota limits and Configure a single-user quota limit.

Voice remixing for Gemini 3.8 TTS models in Preview

Voice remixing is available in Preview for Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS. Voice remixing creates a new custom voice from an existing prebuilt, Extended Voice Library, designed, or remixed voice. You provide a natural-language description of the changes to make, such as a different age, pitch, energy, or accent. To remix a voice, set prompted.base_voice in a Voices API create request.

For more information, see Create a custom voice with voice remixing.

Announcement

Beginning November 9, 2026, the following features will be automatically enabled for Looker (original) and Looker (Google Cloud core) instances running Looker 26.22.

Feature

Looker (original) now supports Google Group mirroring, which lets administrators automatically assign Looker roles and groups that are based on Google Groups membership. The updated Google Authentication admin page also adds advanced role management and programmatic configuration through the Looker API.

Feature

Looker admins can now associate their Looker instance with a Google Cloud project that has a valid billing account. You can specify a Google Cloud project on your instance's Gemini in Looker admin page.

We recommend associating your Looker instance with a Google Cloud project to prepare for future Gemini usage billing, which begins on February 1, 2027. For more information about Gemini billing management, see Manage billing for Gemini-assisted features in Looker.

Note: This release note was updated on November 16, 2026.

Feature

Looker visualizations now support grouping rows or pivot columns that are outside of row or column limits into a consolidated "Other" category. When you use Limit Displayed Rows or Limit Displayed Pivot Columns, select Group remaining rows into 'Other' or Group remaining pivots into 'Other' to display the top N rows or pivot columns alongside an aggregated "Other" category. You can also customize the category label and, for some chart types, choose a custom color.

Row grouping is supported on table, bar, column, line, area, scatterplot, pie, and donut multiples visualizations. Pivot grouping is supported on table, bar, column, line, area, and scatterplot visualizations.

Feature

When you download Looks, Explores, or dashboard tiles, you can include filter and query information in the downloaded file. PNG images can include a filter banner, and Excel workbooks can include query metadata and filter sheets. Dashboard editors can set the default Excel metadata option for tile downloads in the dashboard settings. When you download a tabbed dashboard as a PDF, you can choose whether all dashboard filters appear at the top of the PDF or each tab's active filters appear under that tab's header.

Feature

Looker administrators can now opt in to the official Google BigQuery JDBC driver (Preview) on BigQuery connections. The new driver is built and supported by Google and will replace the current Looker legacy driver in a future release.

To try the driver, perform the following steps:

  1. Open the Connections admin page by selecting Admin > Database > Connections.
  2. Click the Edit button for a BigQuery connection. (See Editing connections for more information.)
  3. Turn off the Use latest stable driver toggle on the connection.
  4. From the Driver Version drop-down menu, choose one of the BigQuery Official [Preview] driver options.
  5. Select Test to check the connection, and then select Update Connection.

Note the following details:

  • Existing connections continue to use the current driver unless an administrator opts in.
  • You can switch back at any time by choosing the previous driver version.

If you encounter an issue during the Preview of Looker support of the official BigQuery driver, report it to cloud-looker-dialects@google.com.

Change

When you download a dashboard as a PDF or set up a PDF dashboard delivery, selecting Expand tables to show all rows makes the Fit Page to Dashboard option unavailable and sets Paper Size to A4, with page breaks enabled by default.

Feature

The Sankey chart type is now generally available. Sankey charts visualize the flow and distribution of data between categories, stages, or states. Sankey charts are especially useful for analyzing multi-step pathways, such as customer journeys, website navigation flows, or resource allocations across different systems. Learn more about using Sankey charts in Looker.

Note: This feature was not released for Looker 26.22, and will be available in a future release. This item was updated on November 16, 2026.

Breaking

Two-factor authentication (2FA) is now enabled by default for all new and existing Looker (original) instances that use email and password authentication and that didn't opt out during the advance opt-out window. Administrators retain full control to manage or disable 2FA by using the Admin > Authentication > Two-Factor panel.

Change

Essential Contacts write operations (CreateContact, UpdateContact, DeleteContact, and SendTestMessage) in the v1 API now generate Admin Activity audit logs (ADMIN_WRITE) in addition to Data Access audit logs (DATA_WRITE). If you have Data Access audit logs enabled for Essential Contacts, these operations generate both an Admin Activity log entry and a Data Access log entry.

For more information, see Essential Contacts audit logging.

Announcement

Apigee Emulator

Apigee Emulator v2.0.3

On November 16, 2026, we released Apigee Emulator version 2.0.3.

This release refreshes the Apigee Emulator runtime and embedded Apache Cassandra base image from the latest Apigee runtime baseline, upgrades Google Guava to 33.7.2-jre, hardens policy execution sandboxes, and addresses 22 container security vulnerabilities across Jackson and the embedded Cassandra Go standard library health-check binary.

The emulator image is available at Artifact Registry.

To upgrade, update the emulator version in your Cloud Code for VS Code settings to 2.0.3. See Manage the Apigee Emulator for details.

Feature

Apigee Emulator

Changed in this release

  • Refreshed the embedded Apache Cassandra (4.0.19) base image to pick up Go standard library 1.27.3 (from 1.27.0) in the /opt/apigee/ready health-check binary and Jackson (jackson-core and jackson-databind) 2.21.7 (from 2.19.2) in the Cassandra layer.
  • Upgraded Google Guava across the emulator runtime, ConfigUtil.jar, and graphql-java to 33.7.2-jre (from 33.5.0-jre), and removed shaded auto-value JARs from the emulator distribution.
  • Hardened the JavaCallout, Script, JavaScript, and Python (Jython) policy sandboxes, and enforced strict OAuth 2.0 redirect_uri sub-resource matching and <EnforceStrictCallbackURI> validation on GenerateAuthorizationCode policies.
  • Incorporated Apigee runtime fixes and policy enhancements through 1-18-0-apigee-9, including Server-Sent Events (SSE) EventFlow lifecycle flow variables (response.event.stream.state and response.event.stream.content.length), <ProxyOperationMode>MCP proxy recognition, LLMTokenQuota semantic-cache-hit exclusion, SanitizeUserPrompt and SanitizeModelResponse MA-Client-Correlation-Id header forwarding, and OASValidation compiled specification caching.

Cloud Load Balancing has entered Phase 2 of the rollout for TLS post-quantum key exchange support across Application Load Balancers and external proxy Network Load Balancers.

In Phase 2 (October 2026 through October 2027), TLS post-quantum key exchange is enabled by default. If you require additional testing or encounter issues with client and intermediate network device negotiation, you can elect to defer (opt out) by configuring SSL policies.

The following is the rollout summary:

  • Phase 1 (Until October 2026): Post-quantum key exchange was available as an opt-in feature configured by using an SSL policy.

  • Phase 2 (October 2026 – October 2027): Enabled by default, with an option for customers to defer if necessary by using an SSL policy.

  • Phase 3 (After October 2027): Post-quantum key exchange will be enabled always, and deferral options will no longer be effective.

Dialogflow

Breaking

Dialogflow's default mutual TLS (mTLS) client certificate for webhook and Dialogflow CX tool requests is moving from Google Trust Services (CN=*.dialogflow.com) to SSL.com (CN=Google LLC). The legacy Google Trust Services certificate remains available only as a temporary fallback until December 1, 2026; update your server's trust store (and any certificate subject allowlists) to trust SSL.com Root Certification Authority RSA before that date. For details, see the mTLS documentation for Dialogflow CX and Dialogflow ES.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is available in AlphaEvolve

AlphaEvolve experiments can generate candidate programs with Gemini 4 Hydrogen in the global, us, and eu regions. To use Gemini 4 Hydrogen, specify gemini-4-hydrogen in Generation settings. Gemini 4 Hydrogen doesn't replace the default model.

For more information, see Supported models, Default model, and AlphaEvolve limitations.

Change

Gemini Enterprise: Antigravity teamwork setting also controls the /swarm command

In the Google Cloud console, the /teamwork-preview command setting in the Features section of the AI developer tools settings is renamed to /teamwork command, which matches the name of the Google Antigravity command. In supported versions of Antigravity, the setting also controls the /swarm command, which lets users run a team of agents that coordinate through a shared message board. When the setting is turned off, users in your organization can't use either command.

For more information, see Configure feature settings.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

Deferred tier for autonomous agent scheduling is generally available

Autonomous agent scheduling (the deferred tier) is available in General Availability (GA) and now supports Agent Development Kit (ADK) agents (google-adk v2.10.0 and later) in addition to the Gemini Deep Research Agent. Pass ServiceTier.DEFERRED to RunConfig on models configured with use_interactions_api=True to queue latency-tolerant agent workloads during off-peak hours with a 50% discount on model inference pricing across Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).

For more information, see Autonomous agent scheduling and Deferred scheduling in the ADK documentation.

Feature

Deferred tier for asynchronous model calls on the Interactions API

The Deferred tier (service_tier="deferred") is available in General Availability (GA) on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. You can run asynchronous Gemini model calls on the global Interactions API endpoint for custom and third-party agents.

The Deferred tier includes the following capabilities:

  • Discounted token pricing: Deferred model calls are billed at a 50% discount compared to Standard PayGo rates, and deferred requests don't fall back to Standard PayGo. For billing details, see Pricing and billing.
  • 24-hour target and 7-day state retention: Enqueue requests (background=true, store=true) that target a 24-hour completion window. Interactions retain server-side state for 7 days to support previous_interaction_id chaining. Deferred model calls use the Flex PayGo per-base-model request quota.
  • Google Gen AI SDK and REST support: Create, poll, stream, and cancel deferred calls using REST or the Google Gen AI SDK for Python and Node.js. To schedule Agent Development Kit (ADK) agents on the Deferred tier, see Autonomous agent scheduling.
  • Supported Gemini 4 and Gemini 3 models: Supports gemini-4-carbon, gemini-4-argon, gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, and gemini-3.1-pro-preview on the global endpoint. Projects with allowlist access can also run gemini-4-carbon-cyber-permissive and gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive.

For more information, see Use the Deferred tier and Interactions API overview.

Feature

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is available in Public Preview

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 from DeepSeek is available as a fully managed model (MaaS) in Model Garden. It's an update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with improved reasoning, coding, agentic, and visual performance. The model accepts text and image input and supports a context window of up to 1M tokens.

For more information, see DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017.

Fixed

CodeMender updates (v0.22.0)

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  • Execution time limits: Added the --duration flag (alias --timeout) to cm find, cm fix, cm verify, and cm session resume. You can also set the limit with the CM_DURATION environment variable. When the limit is reached, CodeMender stops the run, reports the results found so far, and exits with code 50. On cm find --diff, the --fail-on gate is evaluated first, so a blocking finding still exits with code 1.
  • CSV export and import: cm find and cm report now support --format csv and .csv output files, and cm report import accepts CSV files.
  • Exit codes: cm now exits with code 2 for general failures and for sessions that the prompt injection filter stops. Exit code 1 is reserved for CI gate failures.
  • Bug fixes:
    • Fixed an issue in file discovery where comments or strings that matched test patterns or generated-code markers caused source files to be skipped by cm find.
    • cm report import no longer creates duplicate findings when you import the same report more than once.
    • cm no longer sends Application Default Credentials (ADC) tokens to endpoints outside googleapis.com.
    • cm now warns when commands run outside the OS sandbox, for example with --sandbox=false.
    • The sandbox blocks hash-based Python bytecode (.pyc) files and removes bytecode created during a session.
    • cm removes bidirectional text controls and invisible characters from untrusted text before it displays the text.

For more information, see the CodeMender documentation.

  • Fixed an issue where preflight checks erroneously required the control plane VIP (loadBalancer.vips.controlPlaneVIP) to be in the control plane node subnet when the control plane load balancer mode is set to manual.

  • Fixed an issue where audit-proxy retried audit log exports indefinitely on permanent errors, generating excessive audit logging traffic.

  • Actions: Users can use natural language to search, read, create, and update content across these products, for example to send mail, schedule meetings, share files, and post Teams messages. Announcement

Google Cloud CCaaS 6.33

We've released version 6.33 of Google Cloud CCaaS.

The timing of the update to your instance depends on the deployment schedule that you have chosen. For more information, see Deployment schedules.

Fixed

This release addresses the following issues:

  • Fixed an issue where numbers on the inbound blocklist weren't blocked when calling a direct line.

  • Fixed an issue where Telnyx calls became stuck in a queue indefinitely if a hang-up notification was lost during high-load periods.

  • Fixed an issue where callback calls that were abandoned while waiting in a queue were incorrectly recorded as system failures instead of end-user hang-ups, and didn't maintain their first-in, first-out priority order when transitioning between queue groups.

  • Fixed an issue where the call adapter incorrectly redialed a call immediately after hang-up, causing the participant status to fail and the mandatory disposition panel to close prematurely.

  • Fixed an issue where auto-answer calls entered an infinite re-offer loop to the same agent if a connection timeout occurred, preventing over-capacity deflection from triggering.

  • Fixed an issue where scheduled callback redials were placed after their maximum deferral deadline, causing calls to reach customers later than promised.

  • Fixed an issue where an agent's next status prematurely cleared and didn't appear in Agent Monitoring if a voice call's wrap-up ended while they still had active chats.

  • Fixed an issue where the logout confirmation dialog on the Agents page appeared in English when the CCaaS portal language was set to French Canadian (fr_CA).

  • Fixed an issue where virtual-agent-to-virtual-agent chat transfers failed if the transfer turn also ended the conversation.

  • Fixed an issue in the Agents view where the team filter incorrectly displayed agents from unrelated teams due to stale data records.

  • Fixed an issue where the {ACCOUNT_ID} placeholder resolved to an empty string during virtual agent chats, causing CRM API request failures.

  • Fixed an issue where large, unbounded date range queries on the Manager API calls endpoint caused request timeouts. Requests to this endpoint now require a bounded date range.

  • Fixed an issue where loading holiday settings or ending a call in the agent desktop caused significant system slowness due to inefficient database lookups.

  • Fixed an issue where retrieving agent call history caused significant performance delays and system instability.

Google Cloud Contact Center as a Service

Fixed

This release addresses the following issues:

  • Fixed an issue where mobile app chats remained stuck in an Ongoing status indefinitely if a system failover occurred at the moment the chat was scheduled to time out.

  • Fixed an issue where outbound media attachments incorrectly remained in a pending upload state even after a CRM upload failure.

  • Fixed an issue where voicemails were incorrectly attributed to the target agent instead of the destination queue during nested overcapacity deflections.

  • Fixed an issue where advanced call scheduling accepted bookings after a slot reached its static capacity, particularly for requests made seconds before the slot started.

  • Fixed an issue where agent-set availability hours were ignored during virtual agent escalations and agent-to-agent transfers, causing calls to be routed to agents outside of their scheduled hours.

  • Fixed an issue where virtual agent call connection timestamps and handle durations were inaccurately reported.

  • Fixed an issue where agents couldn't transfer active SMS chats to other SMS queues despite the queues appearing as available targets.

  • Fixed an issue where reported queue durations for transferred calls were inaccurate because the wait time was reset after each in-queue announcement.

  • Fixed an issue where IVR virtual agent escalations became stuck in a connected state if the redirection request timed out.

  • Fixed an issue where timeouts during agent availability checks caused newer calls to bypass wait limits and jump ahead of older calls in the queue.

  • Fixed an issue where callers became stuck in the primary queue for an extended period when in-queue announcements were enabled.

  • Fixed an issue where callers experienced a request timeout when hanging up during a virtual agent escalation failure or during high server load.

  • Fixed an issue where virtual agent callback calls were incorrectly recorded as system errors when a customer hung up before being transferred to a human-agent queue.

  • Fixed an issue where DTMF digits weren't sent when the browser's localStorage was full, causing silent failures during IVR navigation.

  • Fixed an issue where the call adapter displayed English text for the self-participant suffix and call type values when the language was set to French (Canada).

  • Fixed an issue where custom external storage path templates and filename conventions weren't applied to session-summary exports.

  • Fixed an issue where per-agent and per-team greetings were incorrectly included in global audible settings lookups.

  • Fixed an issue where smart disposition didn't return suggestions due to the retirement of the underlying Vertex AI model.

  • Fixed an issue where callers were disconnected from post-session surveys following a media stream error in the preceding virtual agent session.

  • Fixed an issue where agent transfers into queues configured with both automatic redirection and agent priority overrides triggered unnecessary outbound API calls.

  • Fixed an issue where callers were disconnected when an agent transferred them to a parent queue that used automatic redirection to another queue.

  • Fixed an issue where returning SDK users weren't correctly identified in Salesforce, leading to the creation of duplicate contact records.

  • Fixed an issue where auto-answered voice calls remained held in a cascade group after the group timer had expired.

  • Fixed an issue where inbound Telnyx calls canceled by the caller before they were answered were incorrectly recorded and displayed as Agent canceled instead of end-user abandons.

  • Fixed an issue where high volumes of audible message lookups caused performance delays when accessing call settings, after-hours messages, and CCaaS portal listings.

  • Fixed an issue where agent adapters unnecessarily reloaded custom ringtones after any instance setting change, causing platform instability and connection failures during high-traffic periods.

  • Fixed an issue where simultaneous ringtone requests from multiple agent windows led to significant performance degradation.

  • Fixed an issue where the inactive chat dismissal timer didn't reset after a task virtual agent session ended or was canceled.

  • Fixed an issue where agents remained in a stuck reservation state and stopped receiving new calls if a call was diverted for an announcement at the exact moment of assignment.

  • Fixed an issue where missing display times or photo counts in pre-session SmartActions caused all SmartActions reporting data for an agent's chat session to be omitted.

  • Fixed an issue where administrators couldn't delete cascade groups from queues, resulting in an "Internal server error" and the group reappearing after a page refresh.

  • Fixed an issue where virtual agent conversations ended with a technical error message due to undetected media stream disconnects.

  • Fixed an issue where virtual agent sessions terminated unexpectedly mid-conversation, causing callers to be incorrectly routed to a default entry queue.

  • Fixed an issue where saving custom agent desktop panels caused system instability and connection timeouts for all active users.

  • Fixed an issue where the chat widget didn't launch for users with certain Japanese characters in their names.

Managed Service for Apache Airflow

Announcement

In December 2026, new Managed Airflow images and builds will no longer pre-install site-packages/ray/jars/ray_dist.jar, the Java runtime that Ray uses for Java and cross-language (Python-Java) workloads:

  • Python-only Ray workloads are unaffected by this change.
  • Remote Java or cross-language Ray jobs submitted to an external cluster (such as Ray on Vertex AI or KubeRay on GKE) are unaffected because they use the ray_dist.jar inside the remote cluster image, not the environment's local copy.
  • Only workloads that start a local Java or cross-language Ray runtime directly inside the Airflow worker, or custom code directly reading site-packages/ray/jars/ray_dist.jar, might require action.
  • Existing environments will be affected by this change when you upgrade them to a version or build that doesn't have ray/jars/ray_dist.jar pre-installed.

If you start a local Java or cross-language Ray runtime directly inside an Airflow worker, you will need to manually supply the missing runtime library. Follow these steps:

  1. Extract ray_dist.jar from the exact version of the ray package installed in your environment. For the list of packages in your environment, see Preinstalled packages changelog.

  2. Upload the extracted ray_dist.jar to the data/ folder of your Managed Airflow environment's bucket.

  3. Add the JAR file path to your Ray jobs using Ray's native java_jars runtime environment configuration option.

Announcement

In December 2026, Managed Airflow (Gen 3) and Managed Airflow (Gen 2) environments will start using Python 3.12:

  • New Airflow builds of Managed Airflow (Gen 3) and versions of Managed Airflow (Gen 2) will switch to Python 3.12.
  • Python 3.11.8 will no longer be available in new versions and Airflow builds of Managed Airflow.
  • Existing Managed Airflow (Gen 3) environments will keep using Python 3.11.8 until you manually upgrade the Airflow build of your environment to a build that uses Python 3.12.
  • Existing Managed Airflow (Gen 2) environments will keep using Python 3.11.8 until you manually upgrade your environment to a version that uses Python 3.12.
  • Managed Airflow (Gen 3) builds and Managed Airflow (Gen 2) versions released before this change will keep using Python 3.11.8.

title: Building a Zero-Dependency Open Agentic Website & Conformance Auditor (MVP Profile 0.3)
description:
Publishing an agent network directly on a static HTTPS website — with no central registry and no custom backend runtime — sounds simple until you try to enforce real browser trust boundaries.

While building VeriMesh for the Open Agentic Web Challenge, we implemented the Worldwide Agentic Web Minimum Viable Specification (MVP Profile 0.3) using pure static HTML5, CSS, and isomorphic ES modules (0 runtime npm dependencies). Below are the concrete implementation details and subtle pitfalls we ran into.

1. The Four Static Artifacts Every Open Agentic Website Needs

To make a static site (such as GitHub Pages) discoverable and runnable by peer browser runtimes without a central registry, four public JSON files carry the full contract:

  1. agent-manifest.json — Site-level index declaring brand, networks[] (name, front_man, resolved hocon/.network.json path), llm_router / BYOK endpoint (https://api.otari.ai/api/v1), allowed_peers, and peer_policy.
  2. Resolved Neuro SAN .network.json — Declarative data-only agent graph (metadata, tools[] with name, function.description, instructions, and callable tools[]). No server-side includes or local file paths.
  3. .well-known/nsdeploy.json — nsdeploy-link/v1 exports and imports for peer discovery.
  4. .nojekyll (GitHub Pages gotcha!) — By default, GitHub Pages runs Jekyll, which silently strips dot-directories like .well-known/ and turns .well-known/nsdeploy.json into a 404. Dropping an empty .nojekyll file at repo root fixes discovery immediately.

Live artifacts on VeriMesh:

  • Manifest: https://devbox-zero-ops.github.io/verimesh-agentic-web/agent-manifest.json
  • Primary Network: https://devbox-zero-ops.github.io/verimesh-agentic-web/verimesh_trust_auditor.network.json
  • Linked Peer Network: https://devbox-zero-ops.github.io/verimesh-agentic-web/compliance_fmea_peer.network.json
  • Well-Known Discovery: https://devbox-zero-ops.github.io/verimesh-agentic-web/.well-known/nsdeploy.json

2. Enforcing Trust Boundaries Inside the Browser

MVP Profile 0.3 defines strict privacy and safety rules for peer-to-peer agent delegation:

  • Fail-Closed CORS Auditing: When auditing a remote Open Agentic Website URL in the browser, fetch(url, { mode: 'cors' }) must fail closed and surface the exact CORS/HTTP error rather than routing around origin policies.
  • Explicit Visitor Consent via Native <dialog closedby="any">: Before verimesh_coordinator delegates a regulated FMEA RPN or Web Crypto SHA-256 chain check to compliance_fmea_peer.network.json, the runtime opens a native accessible <dialog> displaying the exact peer network, requested action, and private-context status (sly_data: NONE). Declining cancels execution cleanly.
  • Session-Isolated BYOK Credentials: Visitor-supplied OpenAI-compatible or Mozilla Otari API keys stay strictly in sessionStorage (cleared on tab close) and are never serialized into peer payloads or public manifests.

3. One Isomorphic Module for Browser, CI, and CLI Agent Skills

We kept the 9-gate conformance engine (js/conformance-engine.mjs) and Web Crypto / node:crypto SHA-256 chain verifier strictly isomorphic so the exact same code runs in three places:

  1. In-Browser Live Auditor: https://devbox-zero-ops.github.io/verimesh-agentic-web/ (includes 1-click presets for VeriMesh Self-Audit and Cognizant's official Tidewhistle reference).
  2. CI Test Suite: node --test tests/conformance.test.mjs (3/3 deterministic tests verifying 100/100 conformance, dangling sub-agent detection, leaked API-key detection, and 1-byte SHA-256 tamper detection).
  3. Standalone CLI Agent Skill (verimesh-auditor): Packaged into our 6-skill zero-dependency repository (devbox-zero-ops/agent-skills v1.2.0) and live on Agensi.io. 
# Install all 6 zero-dependency skills via skills.sh
npx skills add devbox-zero-ops/agent-skills

# Audit any live Open Agentic Website from the terminal

title: On-Device Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech in Google AI Edge Gallery
description: Google AI Edge Gallery now supports on-device, offline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities for building developer-friendly voice applications. Developers can leverage ML Kit for optimized Android performance, or use MediaPipe Tasks and LiteRT for cross-platform open-weight model integration. This local pipeline seamlessly pairs lightweight speech models with on-device small language models like Gemini Nano and Gemma 4 to enable real-time streaming transcription and low-latency synthesis.

title: Unlocking Stable On-Policy RL on TPU with Bitwise-Zero Train–Inference Mismatch
description: How we eliminated floating-point train–inference logprob drift for on-policy LLM reinforcement learning across 64 Cloud TPU v5p chips using a generalizable four-part JAX and Pallas recipe in Tunix.

title: TPU Model Design Considerations and Optimization Guide
description: The newly launched AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-codesign guide provides hardware-grounded design rules to help developers maximize performance on TPUs for LLMs and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) workloads. Key principles include aligning reduction and output dimensions to 256 for systolic arrays, adopting LatentMoE to compress routed token traffic, and mapping parallel axes directly onto physical links.

title: Agents are sessions, not requests: size GKE node pools for AI agent sessions
description: AI agent sessions remain active and idle for most of the workday, making traditional one-Pod-per-session allocations inefficient for cluster resources. By using open-source tools like Agent Substrate and AX on GKE, developers can park idle sessions in object storage to release compute resources while maintaining session state. This approach optimizes resource utilization and reduces Kubernetes node costs by up to 40%.

title: Securing Your Agents: A Hands-On Guide to Agent Anomaly Detection
description: This guide walks developers through setting up Agent Anomaly Detection on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform to monitor AI agent telemetry and catch behavioral risks. It demonstrates how to deploy a sample customer support agent, trigger out-of-scope security findings, and configure proactive alerts using Cloud Monitoring and Security Command Center.

title: Distributed LLM Training Across Metros: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText
description: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText enables developers to efficiently train large language models across geographically distributed TPU slices by streaming parameter fragments instead of synchronizing full models at every step. This approach slashes cross-slice communication volume by over 60× and eliminates network stalls, allowing seamless multi-datacenter scaling without degrading model convergence or quality.

title: Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Tunix and Gemma 4 on Google TPUs
description: This post walks developers through training a multi-turn, tool-using LLM agent using Tunix and Gemma 4 on Cloud TPUs. By leveraging agentic Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and asynchronous vLLM rollouts, the approach significantly improves complex reasoning and tool compliance in interactive environments.

title: From Files to Cited Answers in One API Call: Managed Ingestion and SearchDocuments in Agent Retrieval
description: Agent Retrieval in Vertex AI introduces managed ingestion and SearchDocuments to replace custom chunking and embedding pipelines. Developers can now import document and video files directly from Cloud Storage and query them with a single API call for cited page numbers and timestamped results. The feature supports hybrid retrieval, metadata filtering, reranking, and multimodal video audio search.

title: Introducing Vercel Security Review
description:
Today, we are launching Vercel Security Review in public beta.

Security Review is a new capability in Vercel Agent, alongside Code Review and Investigation. Once enabled, it scans for vulnerabilities on every push to a team's connected GitHub repositories.

Findings appear as comments on pull requests, are listed in the Security dashboard, and are available via CLI. With your permission, Vercel Agent can also validate and push fixes for findings.

How it works

Security reviews are triggered by GitHub push events, including direct pushes to your production branch. In monorepos, reviews are scoped to the project's root directory. Here is how it works:

  1. You push code to a GitHub repository connected to a Vercel project.

  2. As soon as the push lands, Security Review scans the changed code for vulnerabilities like missing authorization checks or exposed secrets.

  3. Findings are posted to the Security dashboard. On private and internal repositories, Security Review also adds a GitHub check to the commit and comments on the pull request.

  4. You can fix findings by clicking Fix with Vercel Agent in the dashboard, or use the CLI to pull findings and have your own coding agent implement changes.

  5. When subsequent security reviews no longer detect a finding, it is marked as no longer detected in the dashboard, and the GitHub comment is closed.

Each review compares the push against a base and covers only what changed. For deployments, the base is the branch’s previous deployment, so the agent reviews the change against what’s already running. Because it only scans the diff, Security Review finishes in seconds and can run on every preview and production deployment.

What the agent checks

The agent reads the diff along with the surrounding code, traces how the changed code can be reached, checks for existing protections, and rechecks each finding before reporting it. That process is how it catches logic flaws like missing authorization checks, which pattern-matching scanners miss.

Each review also applies your team’s security policies, which you can write in plain language and apply to specific projects or across your team. For example, a policy can require any endpoint that returns customer data to check that the requester owns it. You can also manage policies with the Vercel CLI, using vercel security policy.

How findings are tracked

Each new finding is checked against ones that have already been reported, so the same issue isn’t flagged twice. Every finding is tied to the deployment where it first appeared and changes are followed from there. That means that when a vulnerable change from a pull request is merged into your production branch, the finding is flagged in production as well.

When a later review no longer detects the issue in an environment, the agent marks the finding as no longer detected there.

Acting on findings

Every finding explains the vulnerability and how to fix it, with links to the commit and deployment where it first appeared.

Findings are listed in the Vulnerability view in the Security dashboard, where you can ask Vercel Agent to validate and commit fixes. Findings are also available via CLI, so you can fix vulnerabilities with your own coding agent.

Each new finding generates an audit log event, which Enterprise teams can send to their SIEM through Audit Log Drains.

Here is a demo of sample findings in the dashboard:

Fixing vulnerabilities with Vercel Agent

When Vercel Agent can fix a finding, you will see the option to click Fix with Vercel Agent on the finding page in the dashboard. After you click, the agent confirms the vulnerability still exists, then makes the smallest change that fixes it and updates the tests.

Say a developer pushes a change to an invoice download endpoint, and the lookup doesn't check which organization the invoice belongs to. Within seconds, Security Review flags that any signed-in user could download another organization's invoice by changing its ID. Vercel Agent's fix scopes the lookup to the user's organization:

Fixing vulnerabilities with your own coding agent

You can point your coding agent or other systems at the Vercel CLI to pull and fix vulnerabilities:

Findings in the dashboard also give you the ability to copy details as Markdown or JSON, making it easy to paste them into an agent conversation.

Every code change needs security review

Frontier AI models are making vulnerabilities far easier to find and exploit. Last month, researchers turned two decade-old flaws in PHP core into working remote code execution exploits with relatively little effort.

At the same time, agents are writing more of the code teams ship, and each handles security review its own way, or in many cases, not at all.

With Vercel Security Review, you can scan every push on every project for vulnerabilities by default, using the security policies you set.

What's next

Security Review starts with code pushed to GitHub. Next, we're bringing it to deployments from the Vercel CLI and v0, and to repositories that don't deploy on Vercel. We're also working on suggested fixes you can apply directly from the pull request.

Get started

Vercel Security Review is available today in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams.

To get started, enable Security Review in Vercel Agent Settings. You can choose to run Security Review on all projects, or only the ones you choose. To learn more, read the Changelog entry and the Security Review documentation.

Security Review is billed at the Vercel Agent rate, with model tokens at the provider's rate and no markup, plus $0.25 per million tokens.

Security reviews are free until November 10, 2026. Fixes made with Vercel Agent are billed at the rate above.

title: Diagnose Vercel CLI setup problems with vercel doctor
description:
Vercel CLI now includes vercel doctor, which checks your setup and shows the command that fixes each problem it finds.

It checks the CLI version and install, your login and current team, the project link, and your project configuration in vercel.json. It also reports active incidents from the Vercel status page.

Each check reports OK, Warning, Failed, or Skipped. When vercel upgrade can't update the installed CLI, the install check shows where the CLI runs from and how to reinstall it.

Doctor runs without a login or a linked project, and it never prompts, logs in, or links a project, so coding agents can run it before guessing at a fix. Add --json to get each check's status and suggested commands as structured output.

Update to the latest CLI version and run vercel doctor to check your setup, or read the doctor command reference.

title: Vercel Security Review now in public beta
description:
Vercel Security Review is now in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams. Once enabled, every push to a connected GitHub repository is automatically reviewed for vulnerabilities, and findings are reported in the Vulnerabilities dashboard.

What triggers a review

Security Review runs automatically when code is pushed to a connected GitHub repository. Because reviews start from push events rather than pull requests, direct and force pushes to your production branch are reviewed as well. Every project affected by a single push is reviewed together.

What a finding includes

Each finding records the project, environment, branch, and commit, with a summary, a suggested fix, and an AI-generated severity rating.

Security Review adds its own GitHub check to each commit it reviews. When there's a pull request, it also posts findings as review comments that link back to each finding. On public repositories, finding details stay in the dashboard.

Fixes and resolution

Clicking Fix with Vercel Agent on a vulnerability report hands the finding to Vercel Agent, which proposes a fix and opens a pull request for you to review. Nothing merges until you approve it.

To fix findings with your coding agent instead, use vercel security vulnerabilities in the Vercel CLI, or copy any finding as Markdown or JSON.

Security policies

Teams can write security policies in plain language, for all projects or specific ones, to give Security Review more context about how they build. Set a team policy in Agent settings and a project policy in the project's Security settings.

Limitations

Security Review analyzes source code. It isn't a security audit, and it doesn't perform runtime or penetration testing. It helps you find vulnerabilities but doesn't guarantee your application is free of them.

Pricing

Security Review is billed at the Vercel Agent rate: provider inference at the underlying token rate with no markup, plus the Vercel Token Rate of $0.25 per million tokens (input, cached, output). Reviews run on each push to GitHub, so cost scales with how often you push and how much code changes.

Security reviews are free until November 10, 2026, and fixes made with Vercel Agent are billed at the Vercel Agent rate.

Enable Security Review in your team’s Agent settings, or read the documentation and the announcement to learn more. The CLI command needs Vercel CLI 65.10.0 or later.
