title: Google Search AI Mode Adds Read-Only Wallet Access
description:
Google Wallet connections are starting to roll out, while Drive and Gemini chat context are coming later, with permissions that extend beyond AI Mode.

Google is beginning to roll out an optional Google Wallet connection for Personal Intelligence in Search AI Mode. In its November 23, 2026 announcement, the company said Google Drive and its Gemini app would follow in the coming weeks, bringing documents and conversation context into Search.

Wallet access is read-only. Google says AI Mode can use account information to suggest ways to reduce spending or improve credit card rewards, but it cannot move, manage, or invest money.

The privacy decision goes beyond allowing an AI answer to reference a purchase. Google’s help documentation describes connected-app permissions across its broader Search services, including Maps and Shopping. Users should review both the information they are connecting and the services permitted to access it.

What Google Search AI Mode Gets Now and Later

Google Search AI Mode’s November update starts with Wallet, while Drive, Gemini-app context, and a new context-review control have later rollout timelines.

Connection or feature Announced timing Intended use
Google Wallet Starting to roll out November 23 Spending guidance, financial milestones, and credit card benefit suggestions using read-only account information
Google Drive Coming weeks Responses informed by documents, spreadsheets, and PDFs
Gemini app Coming weeks Carry context from Gemini conversations into Search AI Mode
Personalization icon Coming soon Show the context AI Mode used for a tailored response

These additions join existing Personal Intelligence connections such as Google’s Gmail, Calendar, and Photos. Google also says AI Overviews and AI Mode will increasingly tailor responses to recent Search context, allowing research to continue across new search threads.

Image: A more tailored Google Search that’s uniquely yours.

Availability needs careful reading. The Google Search Help page already lists Drive among supported Workspace sources and specifies US English for Drive and Calendar connections. The dated announcement, however, places the expanded Drive connection in the coming weeks.

The help page warns that settings are being updated and may differ from what users see. Taken together, these sources support a staged rollout, not a claim that every eligible account has every connection now. Wallet also has regional restrictions, and Google has not provided a complete connection-by-connection rollout schedule.

Google Wallet: Read-Only Access Still Exposes Sensitive Context

Google Wallet’s connection gives Search AI Mode access to information for financial guidance without granting authority to carry out financial transactions.

Google describes three main uses:

  • Spending guidance: Identify everyday expenses that might be reduced.
  • Financial planning: Help map out financial milestones using available account context.
  • Card benefits: Suggest ways to use cash-back categories, travel perks, and reward points associated with cards linked through Wallet.

Read-only access creates an important action boundary: a generated recommendation cannot itself become a money transfer through this connection. Readers still need to evaluate a separate confidentiality question, because spending information can influence the answers Search produces.

The announcement does not specify the complete transaction fields, history depth, or account coverage available to AI Mode. A spending summary should therefore be treated as guidance based on the information the connection can access, not as a verified accounting of every financial activity.

Reward suggestions deserve checking against the card issuer’s current terms before changing how a card is used. That is a practical precaution: Google describes the ability to recommend ways to optimize benefits, but supplies no independent measurement of the recommendations’ accuracy.

Zeniteq’s coverage of Wallet and linked-bank insights in Gemini covers the related assistant-side integration. This Search announcement makes the destination important: financial context can now inform a search answer as well.

Drive and Gemini Add Documents and Conversation Continuity

Google Search AI Mode’s planned Drive connection will draw on documents, spreadsheets, and PDFs, while the Gemini-app connection will carry conversation context into Search.

Drive’s value is the ability to combine information scattered across files. Google’s example is a personalized preparation plan ahead of tax season. The useful step is assembling relevant context into an answer; the announcement makes no promise that the resulting plan is complete or professionally verified.

A practical request, once available, could ask AI Mode to organize a preparation plan using relevant Drive files. Any deadlines, totals, or obligations in that response would still need checking against the underlying documents.

Gemini addresses a different problem: repeating background when switching products. Google says an idea explored in the Gemini app will provide a foundation that AI Mode can build on, with context sharing working in both directions.

The direction of access matters. Users could already opt in to connect Search history to Personal Intelligence inside Gemini. The upcoming connection adds the reverse path, allowing AI Mode to use Gemini-app context. Existing Search-history access in Gemini should not be mistaken for proof that Gemini conversations are already available to Search.

For readers, the intended benefit is continuity across tasks: explore an idea in Gemini, then continue researching it in Search without restating the same background. That convenience depends on enabling another source of personal context.

The Privacy Boundary Extends Beyond AI Mode

Google Search AI Mode’s connected-app settings authorize access across a wider group of Google services, according to the company’s help documentation.

The support page says that connecting Google content apps means “all Search services will be permitted to access” them. Its service list includes:

  • Google Search, including AI Mode and Discover
  • Maps, including Ask Maps
  • Shopping
  • Flights and Hotels
  • Translate and News

That is a broader consent boundary than a single AI Mode conversation. A user arriving through a Search feature should read the permission as applying to the listed Search services.

Permission also needs to be distinguished from deployed functionality. The same help page currently lists Gmail as the supported source for Personal Intelligence in Ask Maps. Its broad access statement is not evidence that every listed service already uses every connected app.

Two separate boundaries therefore deserve attention. Google’s read-only Wallet promise limits what AI Mode can do with money. The connected-app permission describes which services may access personal information. A user can be comfortable with the first boundary and still decide the second is too broad.

The help page also groups Gmail, Calendar, and Drive under Workspace. Since Google is changing these settings, readers should check the actual permission labels presented to their account instead of assuming every source has an identical control layout.

How to Enable, Review, or Disable Connections

Google Search AI Mode connections are optional, and Google says users can turn them on or off through Search Personalization.

The following checklist separates account eligibility, source access, and response review.

Before Enabling a Connection

  1. Check the signed-in account. Google’s help page requires a personal Google Account and says connected-app personalization is available to users aged 18 or older.
  2. Check the prerequisite setting. Google lists Personalized Recommendations as a requirement.
  3. Review the permission scope. Read which apps and Search services the displayed setting covers, especially if Workspace sources are grouped together.
  4. Choose a specific use. Wallet may be useful for spending or card-benefit guidance. Drive and Gemini add different kinds of context, so enabling one is not a reason to enable all three.

To Connect an Available App

Open Search Personalization, select Connected Apps, and choose the sources you want to connect. That is the route specified in Google’s announcement.

Wallet is beginning its rollout; Drive and Gemini should be treated as upcoming unless the relevant connection is available in the account’s settings. Google warns that interfaces may differ while the settings update rolls out.

To Review Personalized Answers

Check important claims against the original source, especially financial figures and information drawn from documents.

Google says a forthcoming Personalization icon below tailored responses will show the context AI Mode used. Because that control is described as coming soon, readers should not assume it is available alongside the first Wallet connections.

Google also says users can correct personalization through a follow-up in the conversation. Correcting an answer and changing an app’s access permission are separate actions.

To Turn Access Off

Return to Search Personalization → Connected Apps and switch off the relevant connection. Google says these connections can be changed at any time.

Recent-Search personalization has a separate role in tailored answers, so review the broader personalization options in Search Settings as well. Disabling an app connection is an access decision; the announcement provides no promise that doing so retroactively deletes earlier conversations or responses.

Zeniteq’s coverage of temporary threads in AI Mode addresses a related session feature. App permissions remain a separate item to review.

Why Personal Context Matters to Google’s Search Business

Google Search AI Mode gains a practical advantage when users can bring existing financial information, files, and conversations into an answer without supplying the background again.

TechCrunch characterized the expansion as an ecosystem advantage, arguing that Google can draw on information already held across services its users rely on. Its coverage also highlighted the privacy tradeoff and the optional nature of the connections.

The strongest supported competitive argument is about access to relevant context. Wallet can supply spending information, Drive can supply project documents, and Gemini can supply the reasoning or preferences developed in an earlier conversation. Combining those sources could reduce the effort needed to explain a task.

The published evidence does not demonstrate superior answer quality against competing assistants. Google’s own help page warns that Personal Intelligence can make mistakes. More available context creates more opportunities for useful personalization, but also makes it important to understand which source influenced an answer.

For users, a focused opt-in is the most controllable approach: connect a source for a clear purpose, review the resulting guidance, and keep the permission only if the benefit justifies the access.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can Google Search AI Mode Move Money Through Wallet?

No. Google says the Wallet connection is read-only: Search AI Mode can use account information for spending and card-benefit guidance, but it cannot move, manage, or invest money. That restriction limits financial actions, while the separate privacy decision concerns allowing personal financial information to inform Search responses.

When Will Drive and Gemini Connections Be Available?

Google’s November 23, 2026 announcement schedules Drive and Gemini-app connections for the coming weeks. Wallet is starting to roll out first. Google’s help page already lists some Drive support, but also warns that settings are changing, so the connection options shown in your account remain important.

How Do I Turn Off an AI Mode App Connection?

Open Search Personalization, select Connected Apps, and turn off the relevant source. Google says connections can be changed at any time. Review broader personalization in Search Settings too, because recent Search context also affects tailored responses. The announcement does not promise that disconnecting an app deletes previous conversations.

Originally published on Zeniteq.

title: Baidu Opens ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview Under Apache 2.0
description:
Baidu’s open-weight preview pairs a one-million-token context with three precision variants, but deployment depends on memory, kernel support and the workload.

Baidu released ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview weights on November 24, 2026, opening a 280-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model under Apache 2.0. The model activates 14 billion parameters per token and supports a context window of exactly 1,048,576 tokens.

The release is an intermediate post-trained checkpoint, not the finished ERNIE 5.5 Flash. Baidu says post-training is ongoing and that feedback from the Preview will inform the official release.

The downloadable weights follow Baidu’s November 11 announcement of ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, which introduced Qianfan API availability and promised open weights later. Developers now have mixed FP8/FP4, FP8 and BF16 options, all with a DSpark draft head for speculative decoding.

The practical distinction is between fitting the weights and serving the advertised context. A configuration can clear the first requirement while falling short of the second.

ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview Specs and Context

Baidu’s ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview is a text-input, text-output LLM built on ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, with the same architecture and tokenizer. Baidu attributes its new capabilities to mid-training and post-training, with mid-training extending context from 128K to 1M tokens.

Image: baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview · Hugging Face.

The official model card lists these specifications:

Specification ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview
Total parameters 280 billion
Active parameters per token 14 billion
Context window 1,048,576 tokens
Input and output Text
Layers 43: one dense and 42 MoE
Experts 512 routed, top-10 selection, plus one shared
Reasoning Enabled by default; returned separately
Weight variants Mixed FP8/FP4, FP8 and BF16
Release status Intermediate post-training checkpoint

Activating 14B out of 280B parameters means roughly 5% of the parameters participate per token. That sparse activation reduces computation compared with activating the entire model, but it does not turn ERNIE into a 14B model for storage or deployment. The serving system still needs access to the full collection of weights.

The text-only interface also matters. ERNIE’s advertised 3D and video workflows rely on code, tools and external assets. The checkpoint itself does not take video or screenshots as native input.

FP4, FP8 and BF16 Have Different Deployment Costs

Baidu’s ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview comes in three downloadable weight variants, with the mixed-precision repository serving as the default. Baidu recommends FP8 or BF16 when the hardware lacks FP4 kernels, and BF16 as the starting point for fine-tuning.

Neural Brew’s November 24 report provides approximate download sizes and summarizes GPU configurations from the vLLM-ERNIE plugin documentation:

Variant Weight format Approximate files Reported GPU configurations
Default Preview Blockwise FP8 with FP4 routed experts 166 GB 1 × 288 GB, 2 × 192 GB or 4 × 80 GB
Preview-FP8 Blockwise FP8 302 GB 2 × 288 GB, 4 × 192 GB or 8 × 80 GB
Preview-BF16 BF16 600 GB Examples range from 4 × 288 GB to 16 × 80 GB

All three include the DSpark draft head. These are documented configurations reported by Neural Brew, not independently tested sizing results. File size is also different from the complete runtime memory requirement.

Why Fitting the Weights Is Only the First Step

The reported 8 × 80 GB FP8 configuration supports up to 262,144 context tokens, one quarter of the model’s architectural maximum. That is a limit of the documented configuration, not a revision to ERNIE’s 1,048,576-token specification.

The distinction follows from how inference uses memory. Model weights occupy one allocation; attention key/value caches and other runtime state require additional capacity. Longer contexts increase that runtime demand, while concurrent requests add further pressure.

For builders, “supports 1M context” should therefore trigger a deployment check, not an assumption that every supported GPU arrangement can serve a million-token request. The same capacity-versus-deployment distinction is useful when evaluating other releases covered by Zeniteq, including Alibaba’s Qwen4-Max Preview with 1M context and Beam LLM’s 501B open-weight model.

Kernel Support Determines the Useful Precision

Neural Brew reports deployment support through SGLang and vLLM 0.32.0 with the vLLM-ERNIE plugin, with the plugin supporting Nvidia GPUs.

The hardware caveat is narrower than saying that every FP4 deployment requires Blackwell. According to the report, the MXFP4 attention-indexer setting in the documented FP4 command requires Blackwell data-center GPUs. Separately, Baidu recommends the FP8 or BF16 repository on hardware without suitable FP4 kernels.

A sensible setup sequence is:

  1. Check kernel compatibility. Choose a supported weight format before sizing the GPU allocation.
  2. Choose the required context length and concurrency. Weight capacity alone is insufficient.
  3. Use BF16 for fine-tuning. Baidu recommends that repository; Neural Brew reports a documented path through Nvidia’s Megatron-Bridge.

DSpark is intended to accelerate decoding through speculative generation: a draft component proposes tokens for the main model to verify. Baidu says its draft head and FP4 expert weights speed up long-running agent tasks with little accuracy loss, but the cited evidence does not provide an independently reproduced speed measurement.

Apache 2.0 Applies to the Preview Weights

Baidu’s ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview weights use Apache 2.0, while ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base remains under a separate custom license. The shared architecture does not make their licenses interchangeable.

Neural Brew reports that the Base license excludes the European Union, United Kingdom and South Korea, and restricts using the model or its outputs to improve another AI system. The Preview’s Apache 2.0 release removes those particular model-license restrictions from the downloadable Preview weights.

That creates a meaningful option for developers in the excluded regions: they can evaluate, modify and deploy the post-trained Preview under Apache 2.0, subject to its notice and attribution requirements. They should not assume that permission extends backward to the Base checkpoint or forward to an unannounced final release.

For customization, Baidu’s BF16 recommendation also gives teams a clear starting point within the Preview release, without requiring them to begin from Base.

What Baidu Claims for Coding, 3D, Documents and Video

Baidu’s ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview targets tool-using workflows that run for many steps, including software development, procedural modeling, professional documents and video production. Baidu says the showcased work was completed end to end inside an agent harness.

The demonstrations and training-environment figures below are company-reported. The cited sources contain no independent reproduction of these results.

Coding and Game Development

Baidu describes an 11-hour coding task that produced a third-person wuxia game in Epic Games’ Unreal Engine 5.8. The model reportedly integrated assets from multiple engine generations and wrote the game in C++.

The consequential detail is how a text-only model handled visual defects. Baidu says problems identified during playtesting, including a hovering character and misplaced camera, were translated into measurable code tests. A growing test suite and playtest feedback then guided revisions.

That suggests a practical integration pattern: provide the agent with structured failure reports and executable checks. The example’s feedback loop is more informative for builders than the elapsed time alone.

Baidu also reports nearly 100 mobile mini-games built from design documents, many using deterministic game-rule simulations so automated playthroughs and searches could check levels.

3D Modeling and Design

Baidu describes two ERNIE agents using the Blender Python API, one building an airport and the other an airliner. The workflow combined procedural geometry, map data, downloaded assets and generated components, then coordinated scale, cameras and animation.

Rendering used Cycles and OptiX, with FFmpeg assembling the output. The model’s role was to write scripts and coordinate a production toolchain; the renderer and supporting tools performed their respective jobs. Teams attempting similar workflows need those tools and asset permissions alongside the weights.

Professional Documents

Baidu says ERNIE was trained in 300,000 workspaces spanning fields such as finance and law, containing 10 million reference files across more than 40 file types.

The intended outputs include spreadsheets, documents and slide decks assembled from scattered source material. The long context is relevant to retaining references and task history, although a large context window alone does not demonstrate reliable retrieval or correct professional judgment.

Long-Running Video Creation

Baidu says the model can gather, generate and arrange material, control pacing and deliver a finished video over one to two hours of agent work. It reports training across more than 150,000 creation environments.

Those durations describe the surrounding workflow, not a single inference request. Builders would still need an orchestration layer to preserve state, invoke tools, manage files and recover from failures.

ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview Benchmarks Need Context

Baidu’s ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview benchmark results come from Baidu’s own evaluations. Its comparison table mixes competitor results from official reports or Artificial Analysis with measurements performed by Baidu.

To avoid mixing those sources within this comparison, the selected scores below are all Baidu-run evaluations, including the competitor columns:

Benchmark ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5
Terminal-Bench 4.0 46.5 40.9 63.6
AutomationBench 61.9 57.2 58.0
BlenderWorld, text-only 79.0 79.2 86.1

The model card’s evaluation notes say models run at their highest available reasoning setting. Baidu uses official benchmark harnesses where available and different agent harnesses across model families otherwise.

These results support a narrower reading than an overall ranking: ERNIE leads these selected competitors on Baidu’s AutomationBench evaluation, trails Claude on the other two rows, and is close to DeepSeek on BlenderWorld. Scores reflect the model, reasoning configuration and harness together.

For deployment testing, reasoning is enabled by default, with reasoning_effort set to high. The model also supports low and medium, or disabling thinking with enable_thinking: false. Those settings belong in latency and quality comparisons, especially for agents that make many sequential calls.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview Run on One GPU?

Yes, the reported mixed FP8/FP4 configuration can fit the weights on a single GPU with 288 GB of memory. That is data-center hardware, not a typical consumer card. Weight fit also does not guarantee the full million-token context, which requires additional runtime memory.

Does Apache 2.0 Also Cover ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base?

No. Apache 2.0 covers the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview weights. The earlier Base checkpoint retains its separate custom license, including geographic restrictions reported by Neural Brew. Developers should check the license attached to the exact repository they download, particularly when moving between Base and Preview checkpoints.

Which ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview Variant Is Best for Fine-Tuning?

Baidu recommends starting from the BF16 repository for fine-tuning. Neural Brew reports approximately 600 GB of downloadable files and a documented fine-tuning path using Nvidia’s Megatron-Bridge. The smaller FP8 and mixed FP8/FP4 variants offer lower-storage deployment options, but they are not Baidu’s recommended fine-tuning starting point.

title: Did they just call it paranoia
description:

title: How Economic News Can Affect the Forex Market
description:
The forex market is influenced by many factors, including interest rates, inflation, employment data, and central bank decisions. For traders who follow currency pairs, understanding economic news can provide useful context when analyzing price movements.

However, economic announcements do not always produce predictable market reactions. A closer look at how these events work can help beginners understand why exchange rates sometimes move sharply.

  1. Interest Rate Decisions

Interest rates are among the important factors influencing currency valuations.

When a central bank raises interest rates, its currency may become more attractive to some investors because of potentially higher returns. However, the actual market reaction also depends on whether the decision was expected.

For example, if a central bank raises rates but signals that future increases are unlikely, the currency may not strengthen as expected.

  1. Inflation Reports

Inflation measures how quickly the prices of goods and services change over time.

Forex traders often pay attention to indicators such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI). Higher-than-expected inflation may influence expectations about future interest rate decisions.

The relationship is not always straightforward. Market participants also consider economic growth, employment conditions, and central bank guidance.

  1. Employment Data

Employment reports provide information about the health of an economy.

In the United States, the Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report is one of the closely watched economic releases.

A stronger or weaker employment result can affect expectations about monetary policy and influence the US dollar. However, traders usually examine the full report rather than relying on one headline number.

  1. Why Market Reactions Can Be Unexpected

A common beginner mistake is assuming that positive economic news must always strengthen a currency.

Markets respond to expectations as well as actual results. If investors have already anticipated an announcement, much of its potential impact may be reflected in prices before the report is released.

Other factors, such as geopolitical developments and broader market sentiment, can also influence the reaction.

  1. A Practical Way to Follow Economic News

Beginners can develop a simple routine:

Check the economic calendar before trading.

Identify which currencies may be affected by upcoming announcements.

Compare actual figures with previous and forecast values.

Observe how the market reacts instead of assuming a direction.

Review the event afterward to understand what happened.

It is also important to remember that spreads can widen and slippage can occur during periods of high volatility.

Conclusion

Economic news is an important part of forex market analysis. Interest rate decisions, inflation reports, and employment data can all influence currency movements, but their effects depend on market expectations and wider economic conditions.

Learning to interpret these announcements takes time. Rather than trying to predict every market reaction, beginners can focus on understanding the information, reviewing historical examples, and managing the risks associated with volatile market conditions.

Forex trading involves substantial financial risk, and economic analysis cannot guarantee profitable results.
